title: Burning the Lifeboat for Warmth
author: How to Teach With AI
source: How to Teach With AI (Substack), July 30, 2026
summary: This article presents an AI-generated analysis of higher education's existential crisis, prompted by the newsletter author. The analysis argues that universities have historically bundled six distinct functions — credentialing, knowledge transfer, socialization, coming-of-age, research, and civic culture — that are now coming unbundled as technology eliminates information scarcity. AI has simultaneously eroded the teaching pillar and detonated the credentialing pillar by making traditional assessments forgeable. Institutions that survive will be those that honestly identify which two or three of those six functions they still provide best. The title metaphor — burning the lifeboat for warmth — describes universities that cling to outdated models rather than honestly confronting which functions they still serve. The piece argues that trying to serve everyone and differentiate on nothing is a losing strategy in the current environment.
points: The university bundles six functions — credentialing, knowledge transfer, socialization, coming-of-age container, research, and civic culture — that are now coming unbundled.
AI has collapsed the value of knowledge transfer (tutoring anything at 3am) and detonated traditional credentialing (essays and exams assumed a human did the work).
Surviving institutions must honestly identify the two or three bundle components they still provide better than alternatives.
Bryan Caplan's signaling thesis meets its acid test: if the degree is mostly signaling and the signal is now forgeable, the product is in genuine existential trouble.
Institutions that avoid the hard question of who they are specifically for are 'burning the lifeboat for warmth.'
quotes: The underlying condition is that the university has been selling a bundle that was only ever bundled because the components were technologically inseparable.
Information is no longer scarce. It has been getting less scarce since Gutenberg, then the internet made it free, and now AI makes it not just free but responsive.
AI doesn't just erode the teaching pillar. It simultaneously detonates the credentialing pillar.
The signal and the substance both got hit by the same weapon at the same time.
The ones that refuse to ask it are burning the lifeboat for warmth.
